title_guess: Financial market (why people lend and borrow), money vs capital market, organised vs unorganised money market, and the three players of India's unorganised money market
recurring_cast: lend/borrow hands in a pale circle (one hand passes a note to the other) with a MONEY pointer: the channel's 'financial market' emblem, shrunk and carried as the head of every tree
FUND SURPLUS / Lend Money tag (blue, left) and FUND SCARCE / Borrow Money tag (dark, right) on the two hands
green bracket tree: Financial market -> Money market | Capital market -> Un-organised | Organised
wavy vertical divider between the two sibling markets
brand_logo (RBI emblem coin with the letters RBI) on the Organised box
pink Un-organised column vs pale-blue Organised column
instrument_sidebar: left rail listing indigenous bankers, unregulated NBFIs and money lenders, the current one framed in blue with a dot-line into the canvas
lender_desk: a lender behind a desk serving a customer (traditional bankers with a laptop, a suited NBFI clerk, a money lender with a money bag)
red % signs climbing a staircase (high interest), used for NBFIs and again for money lenders
big black question marks over the actor whose motive is being asked
running_examples: three reasons to borrow: start a business, grow a business faster, cover unexpected expenditure
two reasons to lend: earn interest, or dividend (dividend falls in a transcript gap)
loan length boundary: money market up to 364 days (spoken '364 days or less'), capital market 'more than 364 days' on screen and '365 days or more' in speech
spoken only: 50 days vs 500 days objection; a new company cannot repay in one year; a delayed client payment leaves salaries unpaid for 2-3 months
spoken only: money market low risk low return, capital market high risk high return
four community bankers on screen: Gujarati shroff, Multani or Shikarpuri shroff, Chettiars, Marwari (kayas)
NBFI services on screen: loan, chit fund, nidhis (South India); insurance is spoken but not drawn

best_moments.why: the 'financial market' is two hands passing a note, tagged FUND SURPLUS / lend on one side and FUND SCARCE / borrow on the other: the definition as one picture, which then shrinks to head every later tree

the three benefits of a regulator are listed under the RBI column and each sends an arrow left into the pink unorganised column, where it ends on a red cross: 'none of these protections here' shown as blocked arrows, not said as a sentence

indigenous bankers: the banker desk sends 'banking services' to a community crowd, and a 'belong to' elbow loops back from the bankers to the same crowd: lender and borrowers are one community, in one loop
a red line from the community to a big-bank logo is cut by a red cross: 'they prefer their own bankers to big banks' as a refused path
red % signs climb a staircase over the NBFI desk, with a big question mark: high interest and the 'why would anyone go there?' question in one image
money lender desk -> arrow -> a labourer in chains beside a brick stack: debt that cannot be repaid turns into bonded labour, as a cause-to-result picture
a red elbow line runs from 'Un-Regulated NBFIs' back to the matching item in the left sidebar: this sub-branch belongs to the unorganised market, linked by a line instead of a sentence
recap: the three players slide into the pink unorganised column beside the crossed-out benefits and a hand-written 'Done!' tick: the whole video folded back into the overview

weak_moments.why: about 95 s with no visual change (130-236 s) while the narrator raises the 'why two markets?' objection, tells two stories (new company, delayed salaries) and states the risk-return contrast: none of it is drawn
the Ministry of Consumer Affairs (an outside check on the unorganised market) is spoken but never shown
the third bullet says 'operating since ancient and medieval times' while the narrator says 'their connections with the community are stronger': screen and speech give different reasons
insurance is spoken as an NBFI service but only loan, chit fund and nidhis are drawn
a real bank logo and real bank names are used as the 'big bank'; BIE must use a generic bank icon
an app promotion overlay covers the lower left of the canvas for about 18 s (518-536 s), partly hiding the 'belongs to unorganised' line
the RBI role is a grey paragraph callout (consumer-protection rules) in letter-spaced text, a book line on screen

doubtful facts to verify before reuse: chit funds and nidhis are drawn as services of unregulated NBFIs, while registered chit funds and nidhi companies come under state chit-fund law and company law; the unorganised market is called 'not illegal' with 'no regulatory body', while money lending is covered by state money-lenders acts

segments.teaches: non-bank financial intermediaries (NBFIs): firms or individuals with no banking licence that still give financial services (loan, chit fund, nidhi) at very high interest; customers go there because banks refuse those with bad credit
